title: Rosalind and the Wreck
premise: Quentin Eriksen, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane brothers' salvage syndicate, is given one way out: find the wreck of the Halvard, a supply ship that vanished into an Alaskan fjord in 1911 carrying a payroll meant for striking miners. When an unprecedented low tide exposes a sea cave that local legend says swallows the greedy, Quentin and his estranged half-sister Rosalind — who arrives claiming a share of their late mother's map — are pulled into a race against the Vane fleet. As six tides tick down to the glacier calving that will seal the route, Quentin must choose between paying his debt with a lie about the wreck's contents or telling the truth: the 'payroll' was never gold, but the miners' stolen union ledger, and returning it means betraying the only family he has left. In the end, Quentin gives the ledger to the descendants of the strikers, torches his debt contract in the cave's rising water, and chooses belonging over survival — while Rosalind, revealed as the Vanes' informant all along, finally chooses him back.
about_author: C. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former marine surveyor who spent nine seasons charting Alaskan fjords before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who mistake the wilderness for an escape and learn it is actually an auditor.

chapters.title: The Debt of Optimists
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Chasing a supercell across the Kenai Peninsula, Quentin totals his truck — the last asset the Vane brothers haven't claimed. Their enforcer, Maren Vane, offers a deal: locate the Halvard's wreck or forfeit everything. Emotional beat: cornered pride; he signs because he believes he's smarter than the sea.

chapters.title: A Map in Her Mother's Hand
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Arriving in Seldovia unannounced, Rosalind carries a water-stained chart she inherited from the mother Quentin never knew he had. She watches him from the harbor bar, deciding whether he's a brother or an obstacle. Emotional beat: guarded longing; she wants family but trusts no one who owes the Vanes.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A glaciologist friend calculates the calving window: the fjord route opens for exactly six tidal cycles before ice seals it until autumn. The Vanes' fleet needs five days to arrive. Quentin realizes the legend's cave is the only shortcut. Emotional beat: cold arithmetic; time becomes the antagonist.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gave Back
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. At the season's lowest tide, the siblings — forced together by Maren's ultimatum — find the cave mouth exposed beneath basalt cliffs. Inside: 1911-era rigging and a miner's tag stamped HALVARD CREW. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread; the legend is inventory, not myth.

chapters.title: The Ledger That Wasn't Gold
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Deep in the cave, Quentin finds the strongbox — empty of coin, packed instead with the strikers' union ledger and paymaster's confession proving the company stole the miners' wages. He understands why the Vanes want it buried. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; the treasure is evidence.

chapters.title: Blood Money, Blood Kin
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind photographs the ledger secretly and transmits coordinates to an unknown number — revealing to readers she's been reporting to someone inside the Vane operation since before she arrived. Emotional beat: guilt braided with justification; she tells herself it's protection.

chapters.title: Maren's Patience Runs Thin
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Maren confronts Quentin at the dock: the fleet sails tomorrow, and if the ledger surfaces without her signature on it, his debt transfers to his person. She mentions a sister he didn't know he had. Emotional beat: humiliation sharpening into resolve; he stops negotiating and starts scheming.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Low Water
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Quentin catches Rosalind transmitting; she admits she sold the location months ago to buy her way out of her own debts. The fight strips them both bare — betrayal, abandonment, their mother's silence. Emotional beat: rupture; blood proves thinner than either hoped.

chapters.title: The Fleet on the Horizon
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Three days remain. The Vane fleet appears early, running dark through the strait, and Quentin must choose: flee with the ledger alone or warn the fishing families whose ancestors struck in 1911. Emotional beat: first selfless impulse; loyalty begins outgrowing fear.

chapters.title: Descendants of the Strike
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. In the village hall, the great-granddaughter of the strike leader reads the paymaster's confession aloud. Old grief becomes new purpose; the town commits its boats to reach the wreck first. Emotional beat: communal ignition; Quentin feels belonging he's never earned before.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Fog
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Someone cuts the village boats' fuel lines overnight. Quentin traces the sabotage to Rosalind's handler — a Vane cousin embedded in town for years. Emotional beat: paranoia; every ally now wears two faces.

chapters.title: Two Tides Left
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. With fuel scavenged and one working skiff, the siblings reconcile just enough to run the route together — not forgiveness, but necessity. Rosalind confesses her handler promised to erase her debt too. Emotional beat: wary alliance; trust rebuilt on honesty about dishonesty.

chapters.title: Running the Ice Gate
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The skiff threads the calving glacier's meltwater channel under fire from the Vane lead boat. An iceberg calves close enough to swamp them; Quentin's seamanship saves them by seconds. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into competence; the wilderness tests and accepts him.

chapters.title: The Cave Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Inside the flooded inner chamber, they find the crew's final messages scratched into rock — men who chose to stay with the ship rather than abandon the strikers' proof. Emotional beat: reverence; the wreck was loyal when no one else was.

chapters.title: Maren Comes Down the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Maren and armed salvagers enter the cave behind them, sealing the exit. She offers Quentin full debt forgiveness for the ledger and Rosalind's silence forever. Emotional beat: temptation at knife-point; the lie would cost nothing but his name.

chapters.title: The Choice at High Water
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. As the tide floods the chamber, Quentin refuses, hands Maren the ledger openly, and declares its contents public — knowing the water will destroy the originals and the copies already left the village by radio photograph. Emotional beat: liberation; truth costs less than the lie once spoken.

chapters.title: Rosalind's Crossroads
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Ordered to prove her loyalty by shooting Quentin, Rosalind instead destroys her handler's transmitter and stands with her brother as the water rises. Emotional beat: identity resolved; she stops being the Vanes' instrument and becomes his sister.

chapters.title: Calving
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The glacier calves on schedule, collapsing the cave entrance with the Vanes' crew scrambling for their boat — alive, defeated, their claim drowned with the evidence they came to bury. Emotional beat: cathartic release; nature settles the account no court could.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Contract
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Washed ashore, the siblings burn Quentin's debt contract on the beach as the village fleet arrives. Maren, soaked and outmaneuvered, concedes the syndicate won't chase ghosts with no paper trail. Emotional beat: quiet victory; freedom smells like salt and smoke.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. At the village hall, the ledger's story is read in full; Quentin is asked to speak and can barely manage thanks. He learns belonging isn't given for heroics but built by staying. Emotional beat: humility; the reward is a chair at the table, not applause.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Stayed
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind declines the money owed her for the original tip-off, using it instead to fund the strikers' memorial. She and Quentin repair their mother's old cabin together, trading truths they'd hoarded for decades. Emotional beat: tender repair; family chosen twice over.

chapters.title: Next Season's Tide
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Autumn closes the fjord. Quentin, debt-free and storm-chasing again — this time for the weather service, with Rosalind as his navigator — passes the sealed cave and leaves the legend alone. Emotional beat: peace earned; some wrecks are best kept by the sea.
